formables.title: the Nordic Union
formables.desc: Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Finland have shared kings, wars and a common heritage for centuries. United, the North would be a power no empire could ignore.

formables.title: the Iberian Union
formables.desc: Twice before the crowns of Castile, Aragon and Portugal have been joined. A single Iberian state would command the gateway between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

formables.title: the United Netherlands

names.totalist: People's Republic of the Low Countries
names.radical_socialist: Socialist Republic of the Low Countries
names.market_liberal: United Provinces of the Low Countries

formables.desc: The Low Countries were one realm before the revolution of 1830 tore them apart. Reuniting Holland, Flanders, Wallonia and Luxembourg would restore the old Burgundian inheritance.

formables.title: the Danubian Federation
formables.desc: The peoples of the Danube basin are bound together by rivers, railways and trade. A federation of equals could succeed where the old Habsburg monarchy failed.

formables.title: Yugoslavia

names.social_conservative: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes

formables.desc: The South Slavs share a language and a long history of foreign rule. Belgrade, Zagreb and Ljubljana under one roof would form the strongest power in the Balkans.

formables.title: the Balkan Federation
formables.desc: For a century the Balkans have been the powder keg of Europe, their small states played against each other by the great powers. Only a federation of all Balkan peoples can end that game.

formables.title: the Baltic Federation
formables.desc: Squeezed between Germany and Russia, the Baltic peoples can only secure their future together.

formables.title: the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
formables.desc: The Commonwealth of the Two Nations once stretched from the Baltic to the Black Sea. Its partition was a crime; its restoration is a duty.

formables.title: the Holy Roman Empire

names.paternal_autocrat: Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation

formables.desc: Charlemagne's crown passed to the German kings and was laid down in 1806. Whoever holds Berlin, Vienna, Prague, Aachen, Munich and Milan may take it up again.

formables.title: Francia
formables.desc: Long before France and Germany, there was the realm of the Franks. Restore the borders of Charlemagne and the old quarrel along the Rhine ends forever.

formables.title: the Roman Empire
formables.desc: All roads lead to Rome. From the Pillars of Hercules to the walls of Jerusalem, the Mediterranean will once again be Mare Nostrum.

formables.title: the Byzantine Empire
formables.desc: Constantinople fell in 1453, but the Great Idea never died. With the City and Anatolia in Greek hands, the Empire of the Romans can rise again.

formables.title: the Greater Maghreb
formables.desc: From the Atlantic coast of Morocco to the shores of Libya, the Maghreb shares one faith, one history and one destiny.

formables.title: the Arab Federation
formables.desc: The Arab Revolt promised a single Arab nation from the Taurus to Yemen. That promise can still be kept.

formables.title: the Nile Valley Union

names.totalist: People's Republic of the Nile Valley
names.radical_socialist: Socialist Republic of the Nile Valley
names.social_conservative: Kingdom of Egypt and the Sudan
names.authoritarian_democrat: Kingdom of Egypt and the Sudan
names.paternal_autocrat: Sultanate of Egypt and the Sudan

formables.desc: The Nile is one river, and its valley should be one country, from Alexandria to Khartoum.

formables.title: the Transcaucasian Federation
formables.desc: The Transcaucasian Federation of 1918 lasted barely a month. With Tiflis, Erivan and Baku united, the mountain peoples can try again and stand against Russia and Turkey alike.

formables.title: Greater Iran
formables.desc: The lands of the Shahnameh stretch from the Caucasus to the Hindu Kush. A new Iranian empire would restore the reach of the Safavids.

formables.title: Turan
formables.desc: From the Caspian to the Tarim basin, the Turkic peoples of Central Asia have been ruled by Tsars and Chinese warlords for too long. United, they can be masters of their own steppe.

formables.title: the Mongol Empire
formables.desc: Seven centuries ago the descendants of Chinggis Khan ruled half the world. The Mongols of Urga, Inner Mongolia, Buryatia and Dzungaria can at least rule themselves together.

formables.title: the West African Federation
formables.desc: The colonial borders of West Africa were drawn by Europeans in Berlin. A federation from Dakar to Lagos would erase them.

formables.title: the East African Federation
formables.desc: The Great Lakes and the Swahili coast are one region, joined by trade for a thousand years. United, East Africa can finally govern itself.

formables.title: the Central African Federation
formables.desc: Rhodesia, Barotseland and Nyasaland share the Zambezi and its railways. Joined together, they would form a strong state in the heart of southern Africa.

formables.title: Greater Ethiopia

names.syndicalist: Union of Communes of the Horn
names.social_liberal: Federation of the Horn of Africa

formables.desc: Ethiopia alone in Africa never bowed to a colonial master. Its rule over Eritrea, Somalia and the coast would make the Horn of Africa one power.

formables.title: the United Congo
formables.desc: King Leopold's Congo was divided by its warlords and companies. Whoever reunites the river basin will hold the richest land in Africa.

formables.title: the United States of Africa
formables.desc: Pan-Africanists have long dreamed of a single African nation, free of every colonial master. Hold the great capitals of the continent and make that dream real.

formables.title: Maphilindo
formables.desc: The Malay peoples of the Philippines, Malaya and the Indies are one nation divided by colonial empires. Maphilindo would unite them in a single archipelagic state.

formables.title: Gran Colombia
formables.desc: Bolívar's republic broke apart in 1831. Bogotá, Caracas, Quito and Panama together would restore the Liberator's dream.

formables.title: the Peru-Bolivian Confederation
formables.desc: Santa Cruz's confederation of Peru and Bolivia was destroyed by its jealous neighbours in 1839. Its time has come again.

formables.title: Tawantinsuyu
formables.desc: The four quarters of the Inca world ran from Quito to the Maule river. Restoring Tawantinsuyu would honour the Andean peoples who have endured four centuries of foreign rule.

formables.title: the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata

names.base: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
names.radical_socialist: Socialist Republic of the Río de la Plata
names.social_democrat: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
names.social_liberal: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
names.social_conservative: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
names.authoritarian_democrat: Confederation of the Río de la Plata
names.paternal_autocrat: Kingdom of the Río de la Plata

formables.desc: Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Asunción were once capitals of a single viceroyalty. The River Plate should have one master.

formables.title: the Union of South American Nations

names.totalist: Union of South American Socialist Republics

formables.desc: From the Caribbean to Cape Horn, South America shares a common struggle for independence. Hold its six great capitals and the continent will speak with one voice.

formables.title: the North American Union

names.totalist: Union of North American Socialist Republics

formables.desc: Washington, Ottawa and Mexico City under one government would create the most powerful state the world has ever seen.

formables.title: the Pan-Slavic Union
formables.desc: The Slavic Congress of 1848 dreamed of brotherhood between all Slavic peoples. Moscow, Kyiv, Warsaw, Prague, Belgrade and Sofia united would dominate Eastern Europe.

formables.title: the European Federation
formables.desc: Napoleon tried and failed; the Kaiser came close. Paris, Berlin, London, Rome, Madrid, Vienna and Warsaw in one hand would finally make Europe a single nation.
